doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Juggling schedules, management and professionalism
summary: Lamb's Brubeck commitments take priority; Arc Management books around his Caffe Lena series and Ria Curley project.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: One part of doing what you do I believe is juggling commitments. Do you have — you have the Caffe Lena thing going and some lessons. Who takes precedence in your — is it the Brubecks that — they get on the calendar first?
Yeah. Yeah. But you know we get the itinerary for the year, are there any conflicts for you guys, because I also do this music with my wife Ria Curley, which is really exciting.

So that and the Caffe Lena gig are my other investments in and love playing. But you know so on the itinerary I just say no I can’t do — or it won’t be formalized, they’ll say does anybody have any conflicts, and they just book around it.
Who books around it? The Brubecks?
Yeah. We have management. They have management, Arc Management they’re called.
Okay well that’s interesting because that happens on every level of gig playing you know, you get a gig then you call the band or you find a band.
Right, “I hope I can get the right guys” and if you can’t —

It makes me think we had an earlier talk about acting professional and all that, because most musicians have lists of instrument players and when they look at it the most skilled person on a particular instrument may not be your first call because of this person might have baggage and you’d rather go with the person who you’re going to be happy being around.

No, I still run into that stuff for sure with the Caffe Lena. So it’s a monthly series and I get a different guest every month. And you know you don’t mess around on this gig it’s not like you show up and hey what do you want to play. This was like you learn this cat’s stuff really well, you know his recordings, you listen to it, you come in. And I’ve had guys show up, “Oh man, oh here’s the charts” and didn’t rehearse, and that guy is like I’d rather get a younger guy or whatever, that he’ll devote his time. So yeah I know what you mean and I agree and I do run into that still.
